quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Roundabout ahead.
Lane ends, merge left.
Turn around.
Curve ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a roundabout is coming. Enter slowly and let traffic already in the roundabout go first.

questions.question: When you see an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Keep moving.
Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not arrived yet.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Only stop at an accident if you are involved or emergency help is not there yet. Keep watching the road and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not stop just to look at an accident.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a main road from a private driveway?

options.text: Honk to warn drivers you are entering.
Stop with part of your car on the road to alert other drivers.
Drive out fast to merge with traffic.
Let pedestrians and traffic on the main road go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and traffic on the main road go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a main road from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the main road go first.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Go through if there is no crossing traffic.
Keep going because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights are at dangerous intersections. Treat them like stop signs and come to a complete stop.

questions.question: What should you do if another car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if it is open.
If the right lane is not open, wait until the road ahead is clear and slowly reduce your speed so the tailgater will pass you.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: If a car is tailgating and a right lane is open, move over. If no right lane is available, wait until ahead is clear and slowly reduce speed. This encourages the tailgater to pass. Never brake suddenly because this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: When there is no stop line or crosswalk at an intersection, where should you stop?

options.text: You do not have to stop.
Slow down to check that traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see 200 feet in each direction, even if you have to enter the other road.
Stop where you can clearly see traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can clearly see traffic before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the closest point to the intersection where you can see traffic coming. Do not enter the other road to get a better view.

questions.question: Is the most common mistake when backing up failing to look both ways behind you?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The most common mistake when backing is not looking both ways behind you. Mirrors do not show you everything. Turn your body and head to look through the rear window to see as much as possible.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing other cars?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic and pass only when necessary.
Get to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic and pass only when necessary.
questions.explanation: Every time you pass, you increase the chance of a crash. If you drive faster than other traffic, you will have to keep passing. Drive with traffic, within the speed limit, and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: What does a sign with this shape and color mean?

options.text: No passing zone
Wrong way
Railroad crossing
Stop

questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs are only used to mark no passing zones.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is moving?

options.text: Yes, if a train is not too close.
Yes, if your car will not damage the gate.
Yes, if you look both ways first.
No, never.

questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at railroad crossings mean you must stop completely. Do not cross until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully raised. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at a four-way stop sign at the same time:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if two drivers arrive at the same time, yield to the driver on your right. You can then go when it is safe.

questions.question: A driver turning left must yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming bicycles just like you would for oncoming cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn. Go when the road is clear of traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by an adult.
Are safe if standing on the floor in the back.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never ride while standing in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never ride while standing in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Special child seats are made for small children. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Children must always be properly secured in a seat.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works the same way as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.explanation: At a flashing red light, you must stop and yield to all traffic that does not have to stop.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Drivers have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to safely cross. They can be marked by horizontal lines, vertical lines, or both. Always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:

options.text: Alcohol does.
Amphetamines do.
Anger does.
Driving with teenagers does.

questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol affect your driving ability similarly. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving like a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours impairs driving like a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: "Highway hypnosis" happens when:

options.text: You stare at the roadway for long periods of time.
You take frequent rest stops.
You sleep too much the night before driving.
You drive short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: You stare at the roadway for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis occurs when you stare straight ahead at the road for long periods and stop watching the traffic around you. This causes you to zone out and can make you crash into vehicles that slow down or stop in front of you.

questions.question: A stop sign is shaped like a(n):

options.text: Rectangle.
Square.
Circle.
Octagon.

questions.explanation: Only stop signs are octagonal in shape. All eight-sided signs tell drivers to stop completely before going.

questions.question: You can prevent alcohol-related crashes by:

options.text: Deciding before drinking that you will not drive.
Saying "No thanks, I'm driving" when offered a drink.
Calling a taxi.
Doing any of the above.

questions.explanation: The only way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe choices after you start drinking.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Only use your mirrors.
Signal as you start to move into the new lane.
Signal 500 feet before changing lanes on residential streets.
Always check your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Other vehicles often hide in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet before changing lanes on residential streets. Signal 5 seconds before changing lanes on a freeway.

questions.question: What causes many crashes?

options.text: Drivers going too fast for road conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
Drivers staying 4 seconds behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for conditions. Always drive at the legal speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curve ahead.
Roadwork ahead.
Merging traffic.
No left turn.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about upcoming road hazards. This sign warns you of a curve in the road ahead.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection. Oncoming traffic blocks your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for a driver to wave you across.
Move forward into each lane as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see all the lanes you need to cross are clear and it is safe to turn.

questions.question: Should you use low beam headlights when driving in fog?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off fog and shine back into your eyes.
